# Detached Studio reconstruction

The native chat path now has a separate `assets_reconstruct_studio_import` operation after CPU staging. It accepts only an owned `jobId`. The production route captures the actual native mutation actor; the controller reads the original sealed stage run and checks its conversation, target, artifact, plugin lifetime and Edit epoch. It observes the original Workspace/creator again rather than selecting another place.

The Store derives the ordered source IDs, mesh export hashes and geometry counts from the original associated packet bytes. A private host admission queues exactly one `asset.reconstruct` command per run. The command and association commit together. Admission uncertainty is latched before the transaction; queued cancellation, dispatched uncertainty, restart and lost acknowledgements never authorize a replacement allocation command. Generic scene enqueue and receipt restoration cannot invoke reconstruction.

The plugin resolves its actual retained sealed receiver, checks packet accounting and exact source metadata before allocating, then obtains the actual `game:GetService("AssetService")`. `AssetTransfer`/`AssetMesh` reconstruct the supported dense geometry. Ownership transfers once into a private plugin registry; no editable object is serialized. At most two transfers remain owned. Each reconstruction is bounded to 128 meshes, 120,000 aggregate vertices and 40,000 aggregate triangles, while each mesh retains the existing 60,000 vertex/20,000 triangle limits. These are Arcane admission bounds, not Roblox quota claims.

Disconnect, unload and changed Edit continuity retire owned buffers and meshes. Every allocation/yield is guarded. Failure after ownership transfer releases the returned meshes; cleanup failure is an unsafe reconciliation condition and permanently fences that owner. Successful resource destruction is not repeated.

Long reconstructions refresh authenticated continuity from their existing batch yields through the same single HTTP worker. An exact executing command/lease is checked against the original durable association, dispatched state, fixed command expiry and still-fresh preceding proof before renewal. Progress returns no work and cannot extend a lease. Its ACK includes server-derived observation/expiry timestamps. The plugin validates its exact identity, unchanged six-second TTL, current UTC and conservative request duration, then enforces that renewal on every engine guard. Late ACKs and expired renewals stop before further allocation; a small mesh must obtain its first renewal before resolving AssetService. Cadence and duration use the official Luau [high-precision os.clock API](https://luau.org/library/#os-library).

The response contains only the original run/command identity, transfer digest and exact source/count metadata, with `imported:false` and `engineVerification:"pending"`. `assets_studio_reconstruction_status` reads retained facts only: `receiptScope:"historical-reconstruction"`, `currentResources:"unobserved"` and `retry:false`. It never allocates or proves that resources survived a reconnect. The existing staging status remains historical CPU evidence.

This connects production dispatch to detached mesh reconstruction. It does not insert a Model/MeshPart, apply placement/scale, create materials, upload assets, establish source/creator/uploader rights, publish, or provide native/customer acceptance. The full delivery goal still requires those boundaries, supported image/material conversion and customer package verification. The upload journal remains uncomposed until a real cross-process resource binding and genuine rights/consent authority exist; a JSON ticket or dummy JavaScript resource is insufficient.

Current engine APIs were checked on 2026-10-15 against the official [AssetService.CreateEditableMesh reference](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/AssetService#CreateEditableMesh) and [EditableMesh.Destroy reference](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/EditableMesh#Destroy). EditableMesh is an Object, not a parentable Instance. No Studio tool or provider was invoked while developing this change.

Verification uses the actual production controller/Store over temporary SQLite and the native loopback route, plus actual production Luau modules with synthetic engine services in the standalone Luau runtime. These tests exercise ownership, late retirement, receipt integrity, durable command association and non-replay. They establish offline behavior only; native allocation, rendering and cleanup remain unverified.

Recorded validation: the shared build passed with 264 explicit product sources. Reconstruction/journal/heartbeat/native MCP/policy tests passed 33/33, including the actual authenticated progress route; selected production controller and native loopback cases passed 2/2. The complete plugin 0.1.9 suite passed 406/406 with no skips using the pinned official Luau VM/compiler/analyzer. Deterministic `build-plugin.mjs --check` passed. Broader hosted CI and packaged/native customer acceptance remain separate gates; no complete product or native Studio verification is claimed here.
